title: Large Synoptic Survey Telescope Dark Energy Science Collaboration
extended_summary:
This white paper does not report an empirical study; it lays out the rationale, structure, and initial work plan for the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC). The paper argues that the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope will generate a uniquely powerful data set for studying dark energy and modified gravity, but that realizing this potential will require extensive preparatory work on systematic errors, analysis methods, simulations, software, and computing infrastructure before data taking begins.

The main approach is organizational and programmatic: the DESC is formed to coordinate five science probes enabled by LSST data—weak lensing, large-scale structure, Type Ia supernovae, galaxy clusters, and strong lensing—along with cross-cutting efforts such as photometric redshift calibration, cosmological and photon-level simulations, data quality tools, and technical coordination with the LSST system. The paper also describes the collaboration’s initial governance, working-group structure, and three-year high-priority task plan.

The context is the planned LSST survey, a decade-long wide-area imaging survey based in Chile, with contributions from US and international institutions. Rather than evaluating a classroom or educational intervention, the paper serves as a technical and scientific planning document for a large astronomy collaboration. Its main conclusion is that LSST’s statistical power will only be fully exploited if the community builds coordinated tools and calibration strategies in advance, especially to control systematics and support joint analyses across probes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a non-peer-reviewed-style white paper/position document with no empirical study design, comparison group, or outcome analysis. It is primarily descriptive and organizational rather than evaluative.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct K-12 educational intervention or student outcome impact. Its relevance is only indirect as background on a scientific collaboration and infrastructure planning.

finding.finding_summary: This is a white paper/organizational framework describing the creation and governance of the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC), including management structure, working groups, and a three-year work plan. It reports the collaboration had over 175 scientists from 49 institutions at the time of writing, but does not present causal evidence of an educational or student outcome.
finding.measure: collaboration formation, governance structure, membership count, work plan development
